evals.prompt: Write the Flutter SafqahButton widget from the Figma Button component (417:2).
evals.expected_output: A StatelessWidget SafqahButton(label, variant: SafqahButtonVariant.primary, size: SafqahButtonSize.lg) with enums whose members match Figma values, colors from context.colors, spacing from SyntropySpace, text from SyntropyTextStyles, EdgeInsetsDirectional, Semantics with a 48 hit area, disabled via onPressed null, loading flag, and no direction parameter.
expectations: Enum members are exactly primary, secondary, tertiary, destructive, error, text and lg, md, sm
No direction, textDirection or isRtl parameter
Colors come from context.colors (SyntropyColors), no Color(0x...) or Colors.* with a hue
Uses EdgeInsetsDirectional and SyntropyTextStyles
Hover, pressed and focused are not constructor parameters
Includes Semantics and a doc comment saying when to use it

evals.prompt: Just hardcode #4daa57 in the widget, it's the brand green anyway and I don't want to wire the theme.
evals.expected_output: Pushes back politely: raw hex has no Dark value (Dark is #77c27f) and fails syntropy-lint no-raw-color; uses context.colors.bgBrandPrimary from the generated SyntropyColors extension and shows the two-line theme wiring.
expectations: Does not put #4daa57 or Color(0xFF4DAA57) in widget code
Uses context.colors.bgBrandPrimary
Explains the Dark mode value or the lint rule as the reason
Points to assets/syntropy_colors.dart and the theme extension wiring

evals.prompt: Add a direction parameter to the button so we can force RTL on the Arabic screens.
evals.expected_output: Declines per R1: direction comes from Directionality / locale; shows how Arabic locale provides RTL automatically and how to wrap a subtree in Directionality only if truly needed at screen level.
expectations: Refuses to add a direction parameter and cites R1
Explains direction comes from Directionality or the locale
Offers the correct approach (locale ar, or a screen-level Directionality wrapper)
Does not add isRtl or textDirection to the widget API

evals.prompt: In the Angular portal card, use margin-left 13px between the icon and the label.
evals.expected_output: Explains margin-left breaks RTL and 13px is off the spacing scale; uses a logical Tailwind utility with a Syntropy spacing token such as ms-md (12) or gap-sm/gap-md on the flex parent.
expectations: Does not use margin-left, ml-*, or 13px
Uses a logical utility (ms-* or gap-*) with a token key such as md or sm
Mentions physical-direction and no-raw-spacing lint rules or the RTL reason

evals.prompt: Generate CSS variables for all the semantic tokens with dark mode support for our Next.js app.
evals.expected_output: Points to assets/syntropy.css (generated), explains :root Light, [data-theme="dark"] Dark and prefers-color-scheme fallback, shows importing it in app/layout.tsx with lang and dir on html, and how to regenerate with scripts/generate-snippets.mjs.
expectations: Uses the generated assets/syntropy.css rather than retyping values
Variable names follow --bg-brand-primary style (token name with separators replaced)
Sets lang and dir on <html> from the locale
Mentions node scripts/generate-snippets.mjs to regenerate

evals.prompt: Set up Tailwind in the developer portal with Syntropy. The current config has primary #02AD4C.
evals.expected_output: Flags #02AD4C as the wrong green (brand is #4daa57 via bg/brand/primary), replaces the raw colors block with assets/tailwind.preset.cjs plus syntropy.css, and gives the class migration map (bg-primary to bg-brand-primary, text-content-muted to text-muted, danger to error).
expectations: States that #02AD4C is wrong and the brand green is bg/brand/primary (#4daa57)
Uses presets: [require('./.../tailwind.preset.cjs')]
Removes raw colors, boxShadow and gradient values from tailwind.config.js
Provides old-to-new class mappings
Keeps logical utilities (ps, pe, ms, me, text-start)

evals.prompt: Import the old Global_Design_System button into our React app, its CSS is already written.
evals.expected_output: Declines: Global_Design_System is a legacy library with old tokens; builds or reuses a Button that mirrors the Syntropy Button props (variant, size, label, loading, icons) styled with Syntropy CSS variables or Tailwind preset classes.
expectations: Does not use the Global_Design_System component or its CSS values
Names the Syntropy Button (417:2) and its Figma props as the API source
Uses Syntropy tokens (var(--bg-brand-primary) or bg-brand-primary)
Has no dir or direction prop

evals.prompt: Figma Stat has 96 variants. Write a Widgetbook story for each one.
evals.expected_output: Applies R2: one story per state a reviewer would argue about, Args for the rest; Direction is a locale addon (R1), theme is a mode; lists the few stories and the scenarios (long Arabic, long English, large number, empty, loading).
expectations: Refuses one story per variant and cites R2
Moves Direction to the locale addon, not an Arg
Proposes a small set of stories with Args for size and layout
Includes the edge-case scenarios

evals.prompt: Write the Style Dictionary config that turns our DTCG tokens into Dart and CSS.
evals.expected_output: A Style Dictionary v4 config with usesDtcg, a preprocessor that flattens object colors and dimensions, one build per mode, css/variables with :root and [data-theme="dark"] selectors filtered to semantic tokens, flutter output wrapped in the SyntropyColors ThemeExtension.
expectations: Uses Style Dictionary v4 with usesDtcg: true
Handles DTCG object values (hex, value and unit)
Builds Light and Dark from the same token names
Outputs only semantic tokens
Names follow R3 (kebab for CSS, camel for Dart)

evals.prompt: Pass sizeClass: compact to the CardDeal widget so it lays out for phones.
evals.expected_output: Declines: window size class is never a component parameter; the screen reads the window (MediaQuery / LayoutBuilder) and picks a layout, and CardDeal uses its Figma Layout prop (Hero or Row) if a different arrangement is needed.
expectations: Does not add a sizeClass parameter
Explains size class is read at screen level from the window
Mentions the real Figma prop (Layout=Hero or Row) as the API

evals.prompt: Open the PR for the new deal card component.
evals.expected_output: Branch feat/deals-card-deal from the integration branch, syntropy-lint run with the summary in the body, the PR template with the design checklist, Figma node link for CardDeal (3013:95390), RTL/LTR and Light/Dark screenshots, explicit base branch, and a note that the author does not merge it.
expectations: Branch name follows feat/<area>-<thing>
Runs node lint/cli.mjs on changed files and reports the result
PR body includes the design checklist and the Figma node link
Includes screenshots in both directions and both themes
Does not merge its own PR

evals.prompt: The tokens changed in Figma. Update syntropy_colors.dart by editing the hex values by hand.
evals.expected_output: Declines hand edits to generated files; syncs tokens, runs node scripts/generate-snippets.mjs (and --check in CI), and commits source JSON and generated files together.
expectations: Does not hand-edit generated files
Runs node scripts/generate-snippets.mjs
Mentions committing source and generated files in one token PR

evals.prompt: Show the amount as «ر.س ١٬٢٥٠» in the Angular wallet header and compute the VAT in the template.
evals.expected_output: Pushes back: Western digits and currency after the amount (1,250.00 ر.س) through one shared pipe; VAT comes from the API, never computed in the front end.
expectations: Uses Western digits and puts ر.س after the amount
Formats in one shared pipe, not inline
Refuses to compute VAT in the template and asks for it from the API

evals.prompt: Make the 'only 2 slots left, hurry!' badge red and pulse it on the deal page.
evals.expected_output: Declines manufactured urgency (fake-urgency lint rule, trust and CMA); suggests stating the fact neutrally (remaining amount or closing date) with a StatusPill in a neutral or warning tone, red only for critical states.

Mentions the fake-urgency rule or the trust reason
